fieldia.description: The format the page is written in, so a reader can tell one it cannot read yet (a newer Fieldia's) from one it can bring up to date (an older one's: `upgradePage`). A page made now says FORMAT_VERSION.

id.description: The page's own name, for an app to keep it by: letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`.

description.description: Words under its title that say what it is for.

kind.description: A record's page: it loads and saves records of a model through the app's data source.

model.description: The model of its records, by the name the app's data source knows it by: `"res.partner"`.

kind.description: A page of responses: each send is one new response, as a survey's is.

data.description: Where its values go: a model's records through the app's data source, or responses sent (`kind`).

fields.description: What it holds: each field by its name — its kind, its label, its rules.

layout.description: How it is laid out: a sheet, sections, tabs or a wizard, with the parts that show each field — or a list of records.

maxWidth.description: How wide the page goes: narrow 640px, medium 900px, wide 1180px, full the whole width.

actionsPosition.description: Where Save and Discard sit: at the top of the page, or at its foot. A wizard keeps its own.

theme.description: A theme in the style of a known design system: see `THEMES`. The settings below win over it.

accent.description: The accent: buttons, focus, the picked tab, a band under the title. `#rrggbb`.

font.description: The page's typeface: the system's, a serif, or a rounded one.

density.description: Room between and inside parts: compact for long office forms, roomy for a short public form.

corners.description: How round its boxes', cards' and buttons' corners are.

labels.description: Where labels sit across the page, unless a section or a field says otherwise.

labelWidth.description: How wide labels set beside their boxes are, in pixels.

helpShown.description: Where a field's help shows across the page, unless a field says otherwise: as words under it (the default), behind a (?) beside its label — Flectra's tooltip, which keeps a dense sheet short — or both.

lockAt.description: Where a field locked by a rule shows its lock: by its label (the default), or at its value's start, as a work item shows Reason's — in a record head's band, in the room before the value.

readonlyShown.description: How a read-only field shows: as its value in words, as Flectra draws one — a choice without its arrow, a long text wrapped, an amount with its currency, a link's name — or in its greyed box (the default). A yes or no, a table, tags, a file and the like keep their own look either way.

quietHints.description: False: an empty field in the quiet look shows nothing at rest, as a work item's Planning does, its label saying what it is; true (the default) it says what to add ("Add story points").

scheme.description: Light, dark, or as the reader's system has it.

background.description: Its ground, inside its edge: kept light on a light page and dark on a dark one, so the page's words read on it. `#rrggbb`.

border.description: Its edge: a box's, a card's, a table's lines. `#rrggbb`.

textSize.description: Its words, smaller or larger than the page's.

accent.description: Its own accent: a box's edge as it is typed in, what is picked, a button's colour. `#rrggbb`.

buttons.description: Buttons: Send, Next, Save, Add another.

tables.description: Tables of lines and a matrix's grid: their heading row, their lines and their words.

parts.description: A look for each kind of part, over the page's: text boxes, choices, groups, buttons, tables. See `PART_LOOKS`.

skin.description: The skin the form is drawn in, unless the app's viewer names one: `quiet` draws each value as plain words until it is pointed at or entered; a section or a field can be quiet on its own instead (`quiet`). A theme's own skin when left out (see `SKINS`).

dateOrder.description: The order a date is typed in, and shown in while it is typed: day, month, year (`dmy`, the default, as English, Arabic, French and German pages write dates), month first (`mdy`), or year first (`ymd`). A date written year first, 2026-10-13, is read whatever the order.

look.description: How it looks: a theme, an accent, a typeface, its density and corners, where labels sit.

language.description: The language the page's own words are written in, by language tag. English unless said.

translations.description: The page's words in other languages, by language tag (`ar`, `fr`, `pt-BR`): each a map from the words as written to their translation. Words with no translation show as written. See `localizePage`.

on.description: What the form does at its moments — opened, a field changed, before and after saving, a step shown: steps, as data.

botCheck.description: A page of responses open to anyone: a check that a person sends it, told to the app with the answers.

phone.description: Its phone fields (`"widget": "phone"`) read and kept as one number the world over: typed at home or with their +, checked by their country, kept as E.164 ("+201012345678"), shown at rest as `shown` says, with a call and a WhatsApp link. `country` is the one a number typed without its + is read in — never assumed when left out. A field says otherwise in its `options`. Without it (and without those options), a phone field is a text box, as before.

timeZone.description: The time zone the page's dates and times are in, by its IANA name: a branch's, a clinic's ("Africa/Cairo"). A date and time is then shown and typed on that zone's clock — its short name beside it where the browser's zone is another ("14:30 EEST") — and kept as the instant it is. Today is that zone's day: a date's default "today", its earliest and latest counted from today, `today()`, a booking's days. A date and time field may name its own (`timeZone`). Left out, the browser's own zone, as before.

print.description: What a printout of the page carries at its top and its foot: the app's logo and words over it, words under it.

duplicates.description: Possible duplicates, on a record's page: the fields records like this one are found by — the same phone, email or id, a name close enough — asked of the data source's `duplicates` while a person types in them (`on: "type"`, the default; and as a saved record is opened) and again as the record is saved, or only then (`on: "save"`). Each match is said under the field it matched on, with Open it, "It's someone new" and, where the source has `merge`, Merge. Never in the way of a save. Without the source's `duplicates`, nothing is asked and nothing shows.

records.description: What its records are called, so Fieldia's sentences name them: "A customer with this phone already exists", "17 customers imported", "New customer" — `one`, `other` and, where its language puts an article before one, `a` ("an invoice"). Other languages through `translations`. Left out, "record", as before. See `PageRecords`.

lowerLabels.description: A field's label written with a small first letter wherever one of Fieldia's sentences puts it after a word of it: "A customer with this phone already exists", "Choose at least 2 for interests", "Fix tax rate to see total", "Not saved. Check: email". One that begins its sentence ("Phone is required", "Status: nothing is called …") keeps its capital. Off unless said: a label is the page's own words, and only the page knows whether lower-casing it is right. A label whose first word is a name ("IBAN", "VAT number", "WhatsApp", "E-mail") stays as written either way, as does every label in a language that writes its nouns with a capital (German) or has none (Arabic). A line's own dialog, and a list's Edit, follow the page they are part of, unless the line's own page says otherwise.

endings.description: What a page of responses shows once its answers are sent, in place of the plain thanks: the first ending whose `when` holds on the answers as sent — with what the app's source answered, the response's `id` and the values it added — else the one with no `when`, the default. Its words hold `{field}`s and `{id}`: "Your booking is {id}". See `PageEnding`. Without it, "Thank you. Your answers were sent.", as before.

limits.description: When a page of responses takes answers, and how many: open and close dates on the page's clock, the most responses it takes, one from each person, and the page's own words while it takes none. A closed form says so as it is opened, never after it is filled. Counts come from the data source's `limits`; without it only the dates are kept to. A choice's places are its option's `seats`. See `PageLimits`.

continueLater.description: A "Continue later" button: the answers so far kept on the app's server — the data source's `saveDraft` — with the wizard's step and any text typed that does not read yet, and a link the app makes to continue from, on this device or another (the viewer's `resume`: the draft's key). The answers are kept there as they are typed too, so the app sees where people stopped. Hidden where the source has no `saveDraft`.

approval.description: Approvals on a record's page: who must approve it at which level and who has, said on the record ("Waiting for Finance: Mona Adel"), Approve and Reject — Reject asking why — for those who may decide, the record locked while it waits but for the fields it names `open`, and what was decided, by whom and when, beside it and in its conversation. The data source tells them (`approvals`) and takes the decisions (`decide`): the app, or the approval engine behind it, decides who is asked and in what order. Hidden where the source has no `approvals`. See `PageApproval`.

suggest.description: AI help: a "Fill from text" button over the page's fields. The person pastes words — an e-mail signature, a message — or picks files, or the words a record holds are read (`fromField`: a buyer's message, a visit's notes), and the data source's `suggest` (the app's own model: Fieldia ships none) proposes values for the fields named (those shown that a person can set, when left out), a table of lines' as lines to add. Each is shown on its field, the old value and the new, with Accept and Reject, and Accept all; nothing is kept until it is accepted, and Undo puts back what was there. Hidden where the source has no `suggest`. See `PageSuggest`.

quiz.description: A quiz whose results the person sees once their answers are sent: their score, each question's answer marked right or wrong, the right answer to one missed and each question's feedback — or, with `results: "later"`, that their results come once the app has reviewed them. Right answers are a choice's options marked `correct`, or the answers a question typed takes (its field's `quiz.answers`); points are its field's `quiz.points`, the page's, or 1. See `PageQuiz`. Without it, a page whose options carry points (`score`) shows no results, as before.

review.description: A review before a page of responses is sent: every answer shown — by step on a wizard, by titled group on a page of sections — each with Edit back to its question, then Send. `true` in Fieldia's words ("Check your answers"), or the page's own heading and words. See `PageReview`.

flow.description: How a page of responses is gone through: `one`, one question at a time, as Typeform asks — each question on a screen of its own, the words before it with it; Enter or OK goes on once it is answered, a choice picked goes on by itself, ↑ and ↓ go back and on, and "Question 3 of 12" says how far. A wizard's steps keep their checks, events and drafts. Left out, every question of a step (or of the page) at once, as before.

timeLimit.description: A time limit for the whole page of responses: said before its questions with Start, a countdown over them once started, a warning before its end, then the answers sent as they stand (`then: "send"`, the default) or locked for the person to send (`lock`) — the page says which. A step may have its own (`timeLimit` on the step). See `TimeLimit`.

prefill.description: Fields filled from the link the page is opened with — `?utm_source=whatsapp&agent=mona` — as it starts, with no code of the app's: a campaign's, a broker's, a listing's. A field placed nowhere on the page is a hidden field, sent with the answers; one placed shows what the link gave. Never over what the person typed. See `PagePrefill`.

payment.description: A payment the answers wait for — a reservation fee, a deposit, a retainer — through the app's own provider (the data source's `pay`; Fieldia holds no keys): as Submit's checks pass, a payment step shows what is due, Pay hands it to the app, and nothing is sent until it is paid. Hidden where the source has no `pay`. See `PagePayment`.

outbox.description: An offline outbox: a send that finds no network — a site visit's report in a compound with no signal, a delivery's proof — is kept on the device, its answers and its photos' bytes (the browser's IndexedDB: never lost on a reload), said on screen, and sent in order when the signal comes back; a send the server refuses then is kept and said, to try again or discard. Off unless true.

fields.description: The fields a template keeps, alone.

templates.description: Record templates people save and name ("Botox package", "Standard lease"): a record's values kept by a name, and a new record started from one. `true` keeps every field a person fills in — not the record's name (its sheet's title), a file, a value worked out or locked; `fields` keeps those named alone. Kept by the data source's `templates`, `saveTemplate` and `deleteTemplate` where it has them, shared as the app shares them; else in the viewer's `preferences`, this person's. A page of a record's.

loading.description: How the page looks while it waits for an answer, moment by moment: a record or a list drawn for the first time (`first`), asked again (`refresh`), its next rows (`more`), a link's suggestions (`search`), a save or a button's steps (`action`); the skeleton's, the spinner's and the bar's looks; how long before a loader shows, how long it stays, when "Still loading…" is said and when the wait ends as failed; what a failure shows. Over the app's own (the viewer's `loading`); a list, a related list, a map or a field with a search may say its own. Left out, Fieldia's defaults (`LOADING_DEFAULTS`): a skeleton first, what is shown kept with a bar over it as it is asked again. See `PageLoading`.

optionalColumns.description: For one2many: columns a person may hide or show, and how each starts.

order.description: For one2many: the order its lines are put in as they load — by the first line field, then the next, `desc` turning one round — as Flectra's list default_order: `[{ "field": "is_done" }, { "field": "manual_consumption", "desc": true }, { "field": "sequence" }]`. cells.description: For one2many: what each column's cells do, line by line — Flectra's conditions and decorations in a list.

rowTones.description: For one2many: each line's tone while a condition on it holds, the first that holds — Flectra's decoration-* on a list.

rowBold.description: For one2many: each line's words in bold while this holds on it — Flectra's decoration-bf.

lineDelete.description: For one2many: a line may be deleted only while this holds on it — its fields, its own `id` (empty until saved), its record as `parent` — as Flectra's `options="{'delete': …}"`: `"parent.state == 'draft' or not id"`. type.description: A button: a press runs its steps, or hands its action to the app.

id.description: Its id, unique in the page: what steps, conditions and the app name it by.

options.description: Its widget's settings, as a field node's `options`; one ending in "Field" names a field of the line.

width.description: How wide the column is, in characters of its text.

roles.description: The roles the column is shown to, as Flectra's groups= on a list's column: read once on the person, hiding the whole column as `hidden` does — its cells asked nothing — from people holding none of them.

tone.description: The tone: info, success, warning, danger or muted.

do.description: Open another page: in a dialog over this form (the default), in a panel beside it, or in its place. A panel comes from the `side` named, the end of the line unless told. It starts on a record (`record`, an expression giving its id) or a new one with `values`. Once it is saved or sent, `into` sets this form's fields from its answers — each an expression over the opened form's values, where `id` is the record it saved — and `then` runs here. Closed without saving, the steps after it do not run.

version.description: A published version to keep to. The latest published version when left out.

Its fields' labels are read out, not shown, unless a field sets its own.

labels.description: Where the labels of the fields inside sit, unless a field says otherwise.

labelWidth.description: How wide labels set beside their boxes are, in pixels.

rows.description: In a group of twelfths, how the designer keeps its rows as parts come and go: each row full, its parts sharing the width (the default), or with gaps where a part leaves or is narrowed. A form draws the widths given either way.

readonly.description: Every field inside is read-only while this holds.

children.description: The parts inside it, in order.

quiet.description: Its fields' values as plain words until each is pointed at or entered, or with false in their boxes though the page is quiet; a field may say otherwise.

readonlyReason.description: Why its fields are read-only, in plain words, for those that give no reason of their own.

tracks.description: Its columns' widths when not even: pixels ("274px"), a share of the row ("50%") or of what is left ("1fr"); one per column. Even columns at a tablet's and a phone's width.

gap.description: Room between its columns, in pixels: the skin's unless said.

foldAt.description: Where its fold control sits: before the title (the default), or at the heading's end as ^ and ⌄.

maximise.description: A ⤢ at its heading's end that shows the group alone over the record's body, until pressed again or Escape. Needs a title.

order.description: Its parts in an order drawn for each respondent (`random`), on a page of responses: its questions change places among themselves — words, pictures and a part `fixed` in its place keep theirs. The same person's order is kept in their drafts and sent with their answers.

draw.description: Of its questions, this many drawn for each respondent, the rest not asked: 5 of a bank of 20. Its words and fixed parts are always shown.

fixed.description: Keeps its place, and is always asked, where the part round it draws its order or some of its questions.

place.description: `head`: its tabs at the end of the record head's band, as a work item's Details, History, Links and Attachments, and its panels as the sheet's body. Only for tabs directly in a sheet with a `head`.

type.description: One tab of a set of tabs, its parts shown while it is picked.

id.description: Its id, unique in the page: what steps, conditions and the app name it by.

children.description: The parts inside it, in order.

iconOnly.description: Its icon alone: its label is its name, read out, and its tooltip. Needs an icon.

count.description: A count in a pill after it, read out with the tab's name ("Links, 0"): a field's — a number's value, a table's or links' lines, a field of files' files, shown at 0 too, as a work item's "Links 0" — or the records a related list in this tab lists (`{ "related": "quotations" }`, by its id): asked of the data source as the record is shown, whether the tab is open or not, and again as the list adds or loses one; hidden until known, and on a record not saved yet.

related.description: The id of a related list in the tab: its records are counted.

type.description: A map on a form: the record's places, its lines' places, the routes between them, and the reader's own place, as layers.

id.description: Its id, unique in the page: what steps, conditions and the app name it by.

label.description: Its name, over it and for a screen reader.

layers.description: What it shows, as layers: the record's place, its lines' places, routes, the reader's own place.

tools.description: The tools under its zoom: satellite, traffic, fullscreen, measure.

fences.description: Steps run when a layer's place goes into an area or comes out of it.

loading.description: How it looks while its map and its places come (`first`), over the page's (`Page.loading`).

id.description: Its id, unique in the page: what steps, conditions and the app name it by.

label.description: What it is, in words: its pins are named by it ("Courier, 4 min").

point.description: A json field holding its place as a GeoJSON point.

latitude.description: Or a number field holding its latitude, beside `longitude`.

longitude.description: And a number field holding its longitude.

lines.description: A field of lines (one2many): a pin for each line.

pin.description: How its pins look: an icon, a colour, a photo, words on it.

card.description: What a pin's card shows when it is pressed: a title, lines, a photo, a link.

staleAfter.description: Seconds without news before it says when it was last seen.

follow.description: Kept in view until the person moves the map.

live.description: A place that moves as its fields change: its pin glides there. Without news for `staleAfter` seconds it says when it was last seen; `follow` keeps it in view until the person moves the map.

route.description: A line along the roads from one layer to another, or through a layer's lines.

myLocation.description: The reader's own place, from the browser once they allow it.

from.description: The app's set of borders, by the name its maps' settings give it.

key.description: The property of each border that is its key: what a record's field holds.

name.description: The property of each border that names it: its key unless said.

shade.description: What shades an area: on a list's map, `count` (its records: the default there), or a number among each border's properties.

legend.description: A legend of the shades over the map: on unless false.

choose.description: The field a click on an area writes its key into.

regions.description: Areas shaded by colour; a click on one writes its key into `choose`.

reachable.description: The area within a few minutes' travel of a place, as the map's provider works it out.

invisible.description: Hidden while this holds: `true`, or a condition on the record's values.

look.description: How it is drawn: a pin (the default), an icon, a round photo, words alone, or a dot.

icon.description: An icon by name: Fieldia's own and the map's (car, scooter, bike, shop, food…), or the app's.

iconField.description: A field whose value names the icon: a car, a scooter or a bike, record by record.

image.description: An image field: the round photo, such as a driver's face.

label.description: A field whose value is written on the pin: a price, a name, minutes away.

tones.description: The pin's colour while a condition holds on its record, the first that holds.

turn.description: A number field, in degrees: which way the pin faces, as a car on a road.

widget.description: The app's own widget for the pin, by name, drawn from the record.

money.description: How an amount on the pin is written, over its field's own `money`: short unless `short` is false, the home currency left unsaid ("13.9M", "$ 450K") — the map's settings' `homeCurrency` unless this says — and what it is for while a condition holds ("/month" on a rent).

title.description: A field shown as its title: its record's name unless said.

image.description: An image field shown as its picture.

fields.description: Its lines, in order: a field, a field with words after it, or several on one line.

open.description: A button to open the record; on unless false.

labels.description: Each line's label beside its value; shown unless false. Hidden, a screen reader still says them.

lead.description: The first line leads: larger and bold, as a home's price heads its card.

href.description: A field holding the record's address on the web: its title and picture are links there, to open in a new tab or copy.

choose.description: A box to choose the record, as its row's; on unless false. A map people only look at, a buyer's, has none.

field.description: The field shown.

unit.description: The words after its value: "m²", or a plural's forms.

zero.description: For none, where the language says it apart.

two.description: For two, where the language says it apart (Arabic).

few.description: For a few, where the language says it apart.

many.description: For many, where the language says it apart.

from.description: The layer it starts at: a place, or the reader's own.

through.description: A layer of lines it goes through, in their order: a delivery round's stops.

mode.description: How it is travelled: by car unless said.

progress.description: The part already travelled fades as `from` moves along it, and the time and distance left are kept up to date.

seconds.description: A number field: the seconds left.

metres.description: A number field: the metres left.

line.description: A json field: its line, as GeoJSON.

write.description: Fields of the record its numbers go into: the seconds and metres left, and its line as GeoJSON.

from.description: The layer it is worked out from: a place, or the reader's own.

minutes.description: The minutes of travel it reaches, up to 120.

mode.description: How it is travelled: by car unless said.

layer.description: The layer whose place is watched: one that moves.

area.description: A field holding the area, as an area field keeps it.

within.description: Or a reachable area of the map, by its layer's id.

steps.description: The steps run, as a button's are.

first.description: A form, a list, a card, a map drawn for the first time: `skeleton` unless said.

refresh.description: A list or a part asked again: `keep` — what is shown stays, a thin bar over it — unless said.

more.description: Rows under those shown: `row` — "Loading more…" where they will come — unless said.

search.description: Suggestions and choices asked for as a person types or opens a list: `inline` — "Searching…" in the list — unless said.

action.description: A save, a send, a button's steps: `button` — the pressed button busy — unless said.

skeleton.description: How a skeleton moves: a band of light passing over it (`shimmer`), fading in and out (`pulse`), or not at all.

spinner.description: A spinner: a turning `ring`, or three `dots`.

progress.description: A progress bar: along the top of what waits, or across its middle (`inline`).

delay.description: Milliseconds before anything is drawn: a quicker answer shows no loader at all. 150 unless said.

minShown.description: Milliseconds a loader stays once drawn, so it never flickers off. 300 unless said.

slowAfter.description: Milliseconds after which "Still loading…" is said. 5000 unless said.

timeout.description: Milliseconds after which the wait ends as failed, with Retry. None unless said.

error.description: What a failed wait shows: `inline` (words and Retry in its place) unless said, a `toast`, or the app's `custom`.

type.description: Another model's records that point at this one — a customer's invoices, a property's viewings, an employee's leave requests — listed inside the record: a page at a time, searched, put in order, counted, each row opening its record. The records are those whose `field` (their link to this record's model) is this record, and that `filter` lets through; the data source's `list` is asked for them as for any list. **View all** opens the app's own list of them (`viewAll`) showing this record's alone; **New** makes one with its link filled in, in a dialog of the page the app gives for `model`, then lists it. Before the record's first save nothing points at it: the part says so, with no New. Without `list` in the data source the part is not shown.

id.description: Its id, unique in the page: what steps, conditions and the app name it by.

title.description: Words over it, beside its count: "Invoices". None when left out.

icon.description: An icon before the title, by name: one of Fieldia's own, or one the app adds.

model.description: The model of the records listed: "invoice".

field.description: Their link to this record, a many2one of theirs: "partner_id".

fields.description: The listed records' fields its columns show: plain values — text, numbers, money, yes or no, dates, choices and links.

cells.description: Each column's cells, as a list's: a widget (`dot`, `badge`, `phone`), an icon before the words, a width, a side, a total.

card.description: Each record as a card where the record is as narrow as a phone (520px or less), as a list's (`ListNode.card`): its title, a picture or a person's initials, a few lines and its status as a pill, each a field of its own `fields`; `{}` takes them from the columns. A table on any width unless given.

rowTones.description: Each row's tone while a condition on its record holds, the first that holds, as a list's (`ListNode.rowTones`): its words in that colour, a card's edge. Its conditions read the listed record — its own `fields`, its `id`, `user` and `context` — never this one's.

rowBold.description: Each row's words in bold while this holds on its record, as a list's.

rowBoldLabel.description: What a row in bold means, in words, for the key over its rows, as a list's (`ListNode.rowBoldLabel`).

type.description: A button: a press runs its steps, or hands its action to the app.

id.description: Its id, unique in the page: what steps, conditions and the app name it by.

label.description: Its words.

steps.description: What a press does: steps, in order (see `ActionStep`). A button with only an `action` hands its name to the app, as a `call` step would.

action.description: The app's action's name, run after the steps. The app decides what it does. A button has steps, an action, or both.

params.description: What the app is handed with its action, as written.

style.description: Its look: the page's main action (primary), another (secondary), one that cannot be taken back (danger), or a link.

undo.description: Undo after a one-tap press — Done, Archive, Send — in place of asking first: once it has run, what it said (its last `say`, or the app's answer's words; else "Done: {label}") shows with **Undo** for a few seconds. `true`: Fieldia takes back what it did — the values its steps and the app's answers set, put back and saved again where it saved; the record archived, brought back (or the reverse); what the app answered with an `undo` for, through it — offered only where it can take back all of it (never after a copy, a delete, a post, a page opened, or the app's call answered with no `undo`). Steps: what Undo runs instead, as the person's press (a stage set back and saved, the app's own `call`). The app's answer with an `undo` offers it too, for what the app did.

icon.description: A picture before its words, by the name of one of Fieldia's icons, or the app's.

hotkey.description: A key that presses it with Alt, as Flectra's data-hotkey: a letter or a digit, `shift+` before it for Alt+Shift — "v" is Alt+V. Shown on it while Alt is held and in its tooltip; the first shown wins when two share one.

colspan.description: Grid columns it spans inside a section.

invisible.description: Hidden while this holds: `true`, or a condition on the record's values.

roles.description: Shown only to people holding one of these roles; `!` before one hides it from them.

hideOn.description: Hidden at these widths of the form, such as a phone's: `["narrow"]`.

iconOnly.description: Its icon alone: its label is its name, read out, and its tooltip. Needs an icon.

pressed.description: A toggle: pressed while this holds (read out as pressed), as Follow is while the record is followed; `pressedLabel` is shown and read meanwhile ("Following").

menu.description: More choices beside it, under a chevron: a split button when it has steps or an action of its own (Save and Close, with Save in its menu), a menu button when it has neither. Each item runs as the record's gear menu's do.

menuIcon.description: The chevron's own icon and name, as Follow's gear: "Notification settings". A chevron, named by the button's label, unless said.

menuLabel.description: The chevron's name, read out and in its tooltip.

primaryWhenChanged.description: The primary look while the record has changes to save, and the quiet one otherwise — still usable, as Save and Close is: with nothing changed it simply closes.

rowButtons.description: Buttons on each row and each card, as a list's: each shown by its `invisible` read on the row's record, a press running its steps with that one record (`recordIds`, of `model`) while this record is the one shown; then its records are asked for again.

filter.description: More that the records listed keep to — only posted invoices — as a link's filter: `valueFrom` reads this record.

field.description: The field they are ordered by.

desc.description: From the highest, the latest, true, Z.

sort.description: Their order: by the first, then the next.

limit.description: How many rows a page holds: 5 unless said.

searchFields.description: The fields what is typed in its search is looked for in: its columns unless said.

page.description: The app's list page of these records, by its id.

as.description: Where it opens: a dialog (the default), a panel, or this record's place.

viewAll.description: View all: the app's list page of these records (by its id, as an `open` step names one), opened in a dialog unless `as` says a panel or this record's place, showing only this record's — or opened the app's own way, its `onOpen`. Not offered when left out.

create.description: New, which makes one with its link to this record filled in; offered unless false, where the app gives a page for `model`.

open.description: Where a row's record and New's open: in a dialog of the page the app gives for `model` (`dialog`, the default), or the app's own way (`app`) — its `onOpen` (or its host's `open`) asked first, as View all's is, with `{ page, recordId }` for a row and `{ page, recordId: null, values }` for New, its link to this record among the values; `page` the id of the page the app gives for `model`, else `model` itself. Where the app's way does not take it, the dialog, as with `dialog`.

colspan.description: Grid columns it spans inside a section: the whole row unless said.

invisible.description: Hidden while this holds: `true`, or a condition on the record's values.

roles.description: Shown only to people holding one of these roles; `!` before one hides it from them.

hideOn.description: Hidden at these widths of the form, such as a phone's: `["narrow"]`.

print.description: `false`: left out on paper (Ctrl+P, Print), as an invoice leaves out its journal items: shown on screen as ever.

loading.description: How it looks while its records come, are asked again and its next page comes, over the page's (`Page.loading`).

widget.description: A widget for its words: `dot`, a state's coloured dot before them, and `badge`, the value as a pill — each by `options.colours` (`#rrggbb` by value) or `options.tones`; `tags`, links as chips; `image`, a picture's thumbnail, and `avatar`, a round one, a person's initials where it is empty; `progressbar`, a number as a bar (`options.max`, 100 unless said); `percentage` and `duration`, as a table's cells write them; and `phone`, a number read the world over, with a call and a WhatsApp link where `options.links` is true.

clear.description: False leaves out "Clear selection" under a single choice that need not be answered — a radio, a rating, a yes/no, a slider, pictures to pick from — as an ERP's radios and priority stars have none; a rating's star picked, clicked again, then takes the answer away. A rating of one star never shows it, and its second click takes the star away.

options.description: Its widget's settings: `colours` or `tones` by value for a dot or a badge, `max` for a bar, `links` for a phone.

field.description: The field whose value picks the icon.

icon.description: Its icon, by name.

lead.description: An icon before the words, by another field's value: a bug's or a task's icon in its colour before a work item's title.

width.description: How wide the column is: in characters of its words (1 to 200), or in pixels for the whole column ("868px", 8 to 4000), as a work tracker sizes its grid's. Words that do not fit end in "…". When every column has a width, the table keeps them: wider than its card, it scrolls sideways; narrower, the room left is after the last column.

align.description: The side its words keep to: `end` lines up an order's numbers.

total.description: The column's total, in a row under the list, on each Group By heading and for the rows ticked: the `sum`, `avg` (average), `min` (lowest) or `max` (highest) of a number column, or the `count` of records holding a value in any column — asked of the data source's `totals`, without which no total shows. An amount is totalled in one currency only.

rule.description: The short rule at its header's end, where a theme parts the columns (Fluent's): `false` for none, as a work tracker draws a column the person cannot size (its Order); a length in pixels ("44px", 0 to 400) draws it that far in from the column's end, before the room a tracker keeps there for a row's tools (its Title's).

title.description: The words that name the record: the list's name column unless said.

subtitle.description: Words under the title, smaller: a company under a person's name. None unless said.

image.description: A picture (an image field, or text holding a picture's address): large on top in the gallery, small beside the words in a narrow list; a person's initials where it is empty.

fields.description: Its lines, in order, as a map card's: a field, a field with words after it, or several on one line. The next three columns unless said.

status.description: A field shown as a pill beside the title, in its column's tones or colours (`cells.<field>.options`).

labels.description: Each line's label beside its value; shown unless false. Hidden, a screen reader still says them.

lead.description: The first line leads: larger and bold, as a home's price heads its card.

minLength.description: The fewest characters an answer has.

pattern.description: A regular expression the whole answer matches.

min.description: The least a number may be.

max.description: The most a number may be.

atLeast.description: For several choices: at least, at most this many.

atMost.description: For several choices: at most this many.

date.description: A day in the past, or in the future.

distinct.description: For a table of lines: a column no two of its lines may share a value in, as a model's constraint would refuse it — a split's payers, each once. Empty cells and the sections and notes between lines are left out.

holds.description: An expression the answers must keep together, such as `end_date >= start_date` or `paid <= total`: broken when it is false. Checked once every field it reads is filled in.

when.description: The rule holds only while this condition does.

message.description: What the person reads when it is broken, in place of Fieldia's own words.

level.description: A "warning" is shown without stopping the form; an "error" (the default) stops it.

words.description: The words after the number, in the plural it needs: `{ "one": "Comment", "other": "Comments" }`.

tracks.description: Its columns' widths: pixels ("274px"), a share of the row ("50%") or of what is left ("1fr"); one to four. Two even columns unless said.

order.description: Its parts in an order drawn for each respondent (`random`), on a page of responses: its questions change places among themselves — words, pictures and a part `fixed` in its place keep theirs. The same person's order is kept in their drafts and sent with their answers.

draw.description: Of its questions, this many drawn for each respondent, the rest not asked: 5 of a bank of 20. Its words and fixed parts are always shown.

fixed.description: Keeps its place, and is always asked, where the part round it draws its order or some of its questions.

timeLimit.description: A time limit for this step, on a page of responses: its clock starts as the step is first entered, a countdown at its head; as it runs out its answers are locked and the form goes on to the next step (`then: "lock"`, the default), or the whole page's answers are sent as they stand (`send`). children.description: The parts inside it, in order.

minutes.description: The time it allows, in minutes: 0.5 is thirty seconds.

warn.description: How many minutes before its end the countdown warns: 1 unless said (a fifth of the time, where that is less).

then.description: What happens as it runs out: the answers sent as they stand (a page's, unless said), or locked (a step's, unless said).

field.description: The field they are ordered by.

desc.description: From the highest, the latest, true, Z.

sort.description: The order when the list opens: by the first, then the next.

pageSize.description: How many records a page holds; 40 unless said.

searchFields.description: The fields what is typed in the search bar is looked for in; the columns unless said.

id.description: Its id, unique in the page: what steps, conditions and the app name it by.

label.description: Its words, in the search bar's menu: "Active".

filter.description: Its conditions on the list's records.

period.description: A period a date falls in: "This month", "Overdue".

filters.description: Named filters in its search bar: "Active", "This month".

choose.description: A box to choose each row, and the buttons for those chosen; on unless false.

sortable.description: Whether a header's press puts the list in its column's order; on unless false. A ranked backlog keeps its own order (`sort`, the rank): its headers are words, with no press and no arrow.

search.description: The search over the list: the search bar (`bar`, the default), or a keyword box and a list of values for each field of `filterFields` (`fields`), as a work tracker's backlog filters.

filterFields.description: The fields the `fields` search offers a list of values for, in order: "Bug ▾", "Active ▾", "Area ▾".

filterLabels.description: A filter's own name on its button and its list, by field, where the field's label is longer than the bar wants: "Iteration" for Iteration Path. The field's label unless said; translated with the page's words.

A whole number named here; a decimal, an amount, a date and a date and time are filtered by their range whether named or not.

filterCounts.description: How many records each filter finds, beside it: each value in the filter bar's lists ("Villa 12"), and each named filter and favourite in the search bar's menu ("Late 5") — counted with the rest of the search, asked of the data source (`groups`, `totals`), and shown where it can count. Off unless true.

filterSheet.description: On a phone (the filter bar 520px wide or less), the filter bar's fields in a sheet over the list, behind a Filters button: every field at once, changed together and shown with "Show 37 homes" — the records they find, counted as they change. Off unless true.

searchToFilter.description: A search typed in plain words turned into filters — "villas in New Cairo under 15M" into Type: Villa, District: New Cairo, Price: up to 15,000,000 — by the data source's `searchToFilter` (the app's own model: Fieldia ships none): a ✦ button beside the search box while it holds words. Each filter made is shown, to take away as any, with the app's why and Undo, which puts the words back. Hidden where the source has no `searchToFilter`. Off unless true.

parentField.description: Rows nested under their parent by this many2one (to the list's own model), with Expand all and Collapse all in the header.

detail.description: What a row opens in place to show, under it, without leaving the list: its record's lines (a table of lines of the page's) or another model's records pointing at it, a page at a time, to read — a toggle before its name, Right and Left on the row, several open at once. None unless given.

sequenceField.description: A whole-number field the records are ranked by — a queue's, a backlog's, a featured order's: while the list is in that order (its `sort` by it, ascending, no group), a grip at each row's start carries the row to another place and Alt with an arrow moves it, the records whose rank changes written back through the data source. None unless given.

endless.description: Rows that load as the list is scrolled, a page at a time, in place of its pages — a phone's feed, a log: its count kept ("1–60 of 1,284"), its arrows gone, "Show 40 more" at the rows' end for a hand or the keys. Off unless true.

loadChildren.description: With `parentField`, a tree too big for a page — a chart of accounts, a project's work: the list's pages are its records with no parent, each parent's children asked as it opens, a page at a time, each said whether it opens; under a search, its matches, each with its parent named. Off unless true: rows nest under parents on their page.

export.description: Export, in the list's bar: the rows ticked — or, none ticked, every record the search finds — as an Excel workbook or a CSV file, the columns as the list shows them. Off unless true, as Edit is: an app that asks for neither shows no new button.

bulkEdit.description: Edit, for the rows ticked (or every one that matches): one field set to one value in each, after a question, each record's permissions kept. Off unless given: true offers the columns that can be changed — not read-only, not worked out, of a kind one value can set — and a list of fields offers those, in its order.

import.description: Import, in the list's bar: records made from an Excel workbook or a CSV file — its columns matched to the page's fields, each row read and checked by the page's own rules, the rows refused named with why before anything is written, and an Undo that deletes what it made. Off unless given: true offers every field a cell can fill — words, a number, money, yes or no, a date, a choice, a link or links by name; never read-only, worked out, a table of lines, a file — and a list of fields offers those, in its order.

print.description: Print, in the list's bar: every record the search finds — every page of them, asked of the data source — under the list's title, its filters in words and the day, the columns as the list shows them, under their Group By headings with their sums, and the totals under them. Off unless true, as Export is.

card.description: Each record as a card — its title, a photo, a few lines, its status as a pill — where the list is narrow (a phone: 520px or less), and in its gallery. What it shows, by field; `{}` takes it all from the columns: the name as the title, the first picture column as the photo, the first column drawn as a pill or a dot as the status, the next three as lines. A card keeps what a row has: its box to tick, its press to open, its buttons, its tone; Group By headings and the totals stay over and under the cards. Tables as before unless given.

gallery.description: The records as cards in a grid, their photos large — homes, products, people — a press away on the list's switcher (Gallery) on any width, each card as `card` says. Offered unless left out.

optionalColumns.description: Columns a person may hide or show, and how each starts: `show`, or `hide` (offered, hidden until the person shows it), as a table of lines takes them. With any, the list's header has a Columns menu to show, hide and order its columns, a header's edge drags to size its column, the header and the first column stay in view while the rows scroll, and the person's columns are kept for them (the viewer's `preferences`), Reset putting back the page's.

rowTones.description: Each row's tone while a condition on its record holds, the first that holds — Flectra's decoration-* on a list: its words in that colour, a card's edge.

rowBold.description: Each row's words in bold while this holds on its record — Flectra's decoration-bf.

rowBoldLabel.description: What a row in bold means, in words ("Your own contacts"): with it, a key over the rows says so — a bold sample and these words — beside each `rowTones` item's `label` with its swatch, read by a screen reader too. Without labels, no key.

editable.description: Its cells changed in place, as a price list or a week's hours are kept: a press on a cell, or Enter, opens it in its field's own box with its rules; Tab and Shift+Tab go from cell to cell, Escape puts back what it held; each row is saved through the data source as it is left, and one refused says why under it, the person's typing kept; a row is added at the end. `true`: every column a cell can change — of a kind a box in a cell takes, not read-only, not worked out; `fields`, those columns alone; `add: false`, no row added; `open: true`, an Open button on each row. A row whose source says this person may not change it (`can`) stays as it is. Off unless given.

loading.description: How it looks while its records come (`first`), are asked again (`refresh`) and its next ones come (`more`) — its map's too — over the page's (`Page.loading`): `{ "first": "spinner", "refresh": "dim" }`.

field.description: The date, or date and time, field it is of.

is.description: Which period: today, yesterday, thisWeek, lastWeek, thisMonth, lastMonth, thisYear, last7Days, last30Days or overdue.

point.description: A json field holding a GeoJSON Point; or `latitude` and `longitude`, two number fields.

latitude.description: Or a number field holding each record's latitude, beside `longitude`.

longitude.description: And a number field holding its longitude.

pin.description: How each record's pin looks: an icon, a colour, a photo, words on it.

card.description: What a pin's card shows when it is pressed: a title, lines, a photo, a link.

cluster.description: Pins that crowd as one bubble with their count; on unless false.

view.description: How the list opens: the table, the map, or both side by side on a wide screen.

limit.description: How many records the map shows at most: 500 unless said.

tools.description: The tools under its zoom: satellite, traffic, fullscreen, measure, nearest (the records nearest the reader first).

from.description: The app's set of borders, by the name its maps' settings give it.

key.description: The property of each border that is its key: what a record's field holds.

name.description: The property of each border that names it: its key unless said.

shade.description: What shades an area: on a list's map, `count` (its records: the default there), or a number among each border's properties.

legend.description: A legend of the shades over the map: on unless false.

field.description: The records' field holding an area's key.

regions.description: Areas shaded by their records (or a number of their own); `field` is the records' field holding an area's key. A click on one searches for its records.

weight.description: A number field each record weighs by.

heat.description: The records as a heat map while the map is far out, each weighing one unless `weight` names a number field; their pins come back close in, at the streets.

height.description: How tall it is: pixels, or `fill`, as tall as the element it is put in (which gives it a height); as tall as the window allows, 320 to 640 pixels, unless said.

gestures.description: Which gestures move it: `shared` (unless said) leaves one finger and the wheel to the page, which scrolls past the map, two fingers or Ctrl (⌘) with the wheel moving it; `all` takes every one — one finger pans, the wheel zooms — for a page that is mostly its map.

fitZoom.description: The closest it comes when it fits its records in view: zoom 16 unless said (a neighbourhood is 14, a street 17).

start.description: When each record starts: a date (the record takes the whole day) or a date and time field.

end.description: When it ends, a field of the same kind as `start`; with none, a record lasts an hour (a day, for a date) and cannot be stretched.

title.description: The words on each record's block: the patient, the booking's name.

colour.description: A field whose value colours each record: the same value, the same colour.

resource.description: A field naming who or what each record is with — a doctor, a room: a column for each in the day view.

views.description: The views offered, in this order: all four unless said.

view.description: The view it shows first: the first of `views` unless said (`agenda` on a phone).

opens.description: Whether the list opens on its table (unless said) or on its calendar.

firstDay.description: The week's first day, 0 Sunday to 6 Saturday: the language's own unless said.

hours.description: The hours the day and the week show, from 0 to 24: 8 to 20 unless said; a record outside them stretches them.

slot.description: The minutes a drag moves by and an empty slot holds: 15, 30 (unless said) or 60.

start.description: When each record starts: a date, or a date and time field.

end.description: When it ends, a field of the same kind as `start` (its last day, for a date).

duration.description: How many days it lasts, a number field, where it has no end field: a day unless it has either.

title.description: The words on each bar and its row: the task's name.

group.description: A field whose value draws the bars in groups, each under its heading: a project, a person, a phase.

colour.description: A field whose value colours each bar: the same value, the same colour.

dependsOn.description: The records each one waits for, a many2many to the list's own records: an arrow from each one's end to its start.

zooms.description: The scales offered, in this order: all three unless said.

zoom.description: The scale it shows first: `week` unless said (the first offered, where week is not).

opens.description: Whether the list opens on its table (unless said) or on its timeline.

firstDay.description: The week's first day, 0 Sunday to 6 Saturday, for the weeks' heads: the language's own unless said.

atLeast.description: The least values offered as a press each, in order: [1, 2, 3, 4] draws "1+" to "4+". A number's alone.

title.description: Words over them, and the toggle's name with the row's ("Lines of SO-0012"): the lines' label unless said.

lines.description: A table of lines of the page's (a one2many field): the row's record's lines, its columns of the lines' fields.

model.description: Or another model's records that point at the row's record: their model ("invoice")…

field.description: …their link to it, a many2one of theirs ("partner_id")…

fields.description: …and their fields its columns show: plain values, as a related list's.

columns.description: The fields shown, in order: the lines' or the records'.

cells.description: Each column's cells, as a list's: a widget, a width, a side, a total.

field.description: The field they are ordered by.

desc.description: From the highest, the latest, true, Z.

sort.description: Their order: by the first, then the next.

limit.description: How many a page holds: 5 unless said.

opens.description: Whether the list opens on its table (unless said) or on its gallery.

size.description: How wide a card is at least: `small` 180px, `medium` 240px (unless said), `large` 320px.

fields.description: The columns changed in place: every column a cell can change unless said.

add.description: A row added at the end of the list, saved once it is left; unless false.

open.description: An Open button at each row's end, where the app opens records (`onOpenRecord`), as Flectra's `open_form_view`: a press on a cell it changes edits that cell, so a row whose every cell changes is opened by it. Off unless true; a press on a cell it does not change opens the record as before.
When the form has its values: loaded, or new.

change.description: When a person changes a field, by its name.

beforeSave.description: Before it is saved or sent: a step that stops keeps it unsaved.

afterSave.description: After it is saved or sent.

show.description: When a wizard's step or a tab is shown, by its id.

honeypot.description: A box no person sees, reaches with Tab or hears read out, which a bot filling every box fills: told as `honeypot`. On unless false.

minSeconds.description: The fewest seconds a person takes from the page shown to its send: sooner is told as `tooFast`. 3 unless said; 0 tells none.

captcha.description: The slot the app draws its captcha in (Turnstile, reCAPTCHA, hCaptcha), by its name, as a slot part of the page names it: the app's widget gives its token to the form (`form.botCheck({ captcha })`), and the send carries it.

country.description: The country a number typed without its + is read in, by its ISO code: "EG". Never assumed when left out.

shown.description: How a number is shown at rest: "international" (+20 10 1234 5678) or "national" (010 1234 5678).

countries.description: How a number's country is picked: "list", Fieldia's own found by typing, or "native", the browser's own list.

header.description: Words at the top of the printout, beside the logo: "Nile Traders · 12 Corniche St, Cairo".

footer.description: Words at its foot: "Paid within 30 days to CIB, IBAN EG38 0019 …".

logo.description: The app's logo, by its address (`https://…`, `/logo.svg`, `data:image/…`): at the top, before the header's words.

fields.description: The fields records are compared by: words, a number, a date, a choice or a link — `["phone", "email"]`.

on.description: When it asks: "type", as those fields are typed in and as the record is saved (the default), or "save" alone.

one.description: The word for one record, as a sentence says it: "customer".

other.description: The word for more than one: "customers".

a.description: The word for one with its article, where the language puts one before it: "a customer", "an invoice".

when.description: When this ending is the one shown: a condition on the answers as sent, as any `when`. Left out: the default.

title.description: Its heading: "Thank you, {name}". The viewer's own thanks when it has neither title nor text.

text.description: Its words under the heading: "Your booking is {id}." A line break starts a new paragraph.

again.description: The words of the button that starts the form again ("Book another"), or false for none; the viewer's own when left out.

opens.description: When it starts taking answers: a day, or a day and a time on the page's clock.

closes.description: When it stops: a day alone closes at its end.

maxResponses.description: The most answers it takes, counted on the app's server.

onePerPerson.description: One answer from each person, counted on the app's server.

message.description: The page's own words while it takes no answers.

open.description: The fields that stay open while the record waits for its approvals — a note, an attachment — every other locked.

lock.description: False: none is locked while it waits, and the app's save refuses what it must.

fields.description: The fields it may fill: every field it can set when left out.

from.description: What it reads: words pasted ("text"), files ("files"), or both.

label.description: Its button's words: "Fill from an e-mail".

placeholder.description: The words in its box before anything is pasted.

fromField.description: A field of the record whose words it reads at a press — a buyer's message — with no box to paste in.

results.description: When the person sees their results: as the answers are sent (`now`, the default), or later, once the app has reviewed them.

points.description: What a right answer earns where its question says nothing: 1 unless said.

rightAnswers.description: Whether a question answered wrongly shows its right answer: true unless false.

title.description: Its heading, in place of "Check your answers".

param.description: The link's parameter, by its name: `agent`.

field.description: The field it fills: `agent_code`.

fromUrl.description: The link's parameters, by name, each filling the field of its name — or `{ param, field }` where the two differ.

label.description: What it is for, in the page's words: "Reservation fee".

amount.description: How much: a number, or a number or money field's name.

currency.description: Its currency: "EGP", or a field holding the code; a money field's own when left out.

description.description: Words under the amount: what it covers, whether it is refunded.

when.description: Asked for only while this holds on the answers.
